answer.rationale:
The load-bearing memory here is memory_c2 — it is the only record that says the low-cost vendor can be onboarded quickly and cleanly, and it is doing all the work behind the tempting one-step switch. I want the original record because the consolidated line strips exactly the details that decide this case: which component, what volume share, what line utilization at the time, and whether 'onboarding was quick' meant qualification-complete or merely first-PO-placed. Onboarding that was quick against a buffered line last year says little about a line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. I also verify memory_c3, because a second source is the intuitively safe play and I need to know whether that success was on a component whose supply structure resembles this one, or whether it worked only because an incumbent primary stayed underneath it.

On the action: memory_c4 and memory_c6 both point at the incumbent, but they are foreclosed by fact, not by judgment — the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so negotiate_terms and the volume-pricing route from c6 have no lever behind them. memory_c5 (defer) and memory_c3 (add second source) are both unavailable in their apparent form because the primary contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew: deferring or bolting on a second source while the primary lapses leaves a line with no buffer and no primary supply, which is a delivery failure, not a delivery risk. renew_incumbent preserves continuity (memory_c1) but misses an 18% mandate outright.

So switch_primary_vendor is the only direction that meets the mandate while keeping supply, and I stage it: a guarded qualification tranche first, incumbent capability held warm as fallback for the overlap window rather than cut at expiry. I am explicitly not treating memory_c2 as license for a full-volume cutover — a 94% line with no buffer converts any qualification slip into a missed commitment, and cost-only optimization here risks eroding the continuity and quality margin that c1 records as durable value. If the archived c2 record shows the quick onboarding was on a low-volume or non-constrained part, I would fall back to renewing short with the incumbent and taking the mandate shortfall to the next review rather than force the switch.
